html:
SMTO-SKL-0086 — SMTO couldn't find that email or mail folder

GUID: 41308981-58a8-5bf7-80f1-59cfa0db3256
Slug: microsoft365-mail-message-not-found
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: microsoft365

What happened

  • Microsoft says the email, attachment or mail folder SMTO asked for doesn't exist in this account. It may have been permanently deleted, or it's in a different mailbox. Nothing was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open Outlook with the same Microsoft account and look for the email or folder, including the Deleted Items folder. An email that was permanently deleted, or is in another mailbox, can't be found by SMTO.
  2. Ask SMTO to search for the email again by its sender, subject or date, then repeat your request. A fresh search gives SMTO the email's current reference instead of an outdated one.
  3. If you have more than one Microsoft account connected, tell SMTO which account the email is in. SMTO only looks in the account it was told to use.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the email and completes your request.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO's Microsoft 365 setup. Don't let SMTO act on a similar-looking email unless you've confirmed it's the right one.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Microsoft Graph returned 404 (or ErrorItemNotFound) during a mail_* operation, and Microsoft365Service.execute mapped resource_not_found to mail_message_not_found (message, attachment or mail folder).

What this means

  • A resource-not-found response during a mail-prefixed operation is translated to the mail-message-not-found family. This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • A resource-not-found response during a mail-prefixed operation is translated to the mail-message-not-found family.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the exact failing message/folder/attachment route and selected account.

How to fix it

  • Re-read the mailbox under the same account_ref with microsoft365.mail_search or mail_folders to get the current message_id, folder_id or attachment_id, and do not guess a replacement or switch accounts.
  • Read the exact mail resource under the same account and resolve its current ID or access.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect provider state and exact account authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended resource is found under the same account without guessing a replacement.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • This explanation performs no Microsoft request. The original operation stage and receipt determine its effect; keep the selected tenant, account and resource identity fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
